purpose: Independent primary-source checks for AWS cost scenarios, outside candidate specifications.
method: Researchers supplied claims and primary URLs. A separate checking agent independently opened each primary page and checked values, units, scope, and qualifications.

final_verification.method: Independently opened the cited primary URLs and rechecked all 19 values, units, scopes, and recorded qualifications after the first source audit.
final_verification.result: All 19 approved wordings are confirmed as qualified. W4's area values are confirmed, but its Great Lakes exclusion remains an explicitly labeled inference.
final_verification.limits: No current Oregon price export was verified. Historical and other-region prices remain planning proxies. Source review does not measure service performance.

checks.topic: NHDPlus HR mapped lake, pond, and reservoir objects
checks.approved_wording: EPA reports 5,304,841 LakePond objects and 280,298 Reservoir objects in its NHDPlus HR source frame. Their sum is 5,585,139.
checks.locator: Table 2-3, printed page 20, PDF page index 19. Independently checked table text and requested the corresponding PDF page rendering.
checks.qualification: These are mapped objects before eligibility screening. They include intermittent water and excluded sizes and types. They are not a permanent-water census.

checks.approved_wording: EPA's sampling frame contains 497,840 lake objects. Its four area bins contain 359,553, 77,086, 46,430, and 14,771 objects.
checks.locator: Table 2-4, printed page 21, PDF page index 20. Inclusion rules appear on printed pages 19 and 20.
checks.qualification: Corrected eligibility wording to sampling-frame objects. EPA excludes polygons at or below one hectare and many artificial basin types. Field screening removes further non-targets.

checks.unit: perennial lakes and reservoirs at least 1 hectare
checks.approved_wording: LAGOS-US LOCUS v1.0 contains 479,950 perennial lakes and reservoirs of at least one hectare across the conterminous United States.
checks.locator: Abstract and Data description, lake definition and artificial-basin exclusions.
checks.qualification: The census excludes wholly artificial or intensively used basins, including aquaculture, sewage, and retention ponds. It excludes smaller ponds required by this scenario.

checks.topic: Published CONUS lake and reservoir area anchor
checks.approved_wording: A published NHD-based CONUS assessment reports 126,793 square kilometers of lake and reservoir area. Its HUC 04 contribution is 7,798 square kilometers.
checks.locator: Table S4 and adjacent lake-area methods.
checks.qualification: The Great Lakes exclusion is inferred from the small HUC 04 area, not explicitly confirmed by this table. This is not current permanent-water area.

checks.approved_wording: NHD was mapped at 1:24,000 or larger scale outside Alaska. NHD retired on 2023-10-01 and remains available without further maintenance.
checks.locator: Opening retirement notice and National Hydrography Dataset section.
checks.qualification: Map scale does not establish complete detection of ten-meter ponds. Alaska has a different stated mapping scale and is outside these scenarios.

checks.approved_wording: Sentinel-2 Level-2A tiles use a 100-kilometer grid step and nominal 110-by-110-kilometer footprints, creating overlap.
checks.locator: MSI Products Overview and Level-2A Products.
checks.qualification: Some footprints contain partial imagery. Nominal tile size does not establish the exact number of CONUS tiles or the number intersecting water bodies.

checks.unit: vCPU, GiB, Gbps, and storage flag
checks.approved_wording: A c7i.xlarge provides four vCPUs and eight GiB of memory. It uses EBS storage with advertised network bandwidth up to 12.5 Gbps.
checks.qualification: Advertised maxima are not sustained workload throughput. Four vCPUs do not establish fourfold acceleration for a serial extraction worker.

checks.unit: USD per c7i.xlarge instance-hour, On-Demand us-west-2, November 2023
checks.approved_wording: An AWS benchmark lists Oregon c7i.xlarge On-Demand pricing at $0.1785 per instance-hour as of November 2023.
checks.locator: Hourly cost comparison table and November 2023 price note. Article published 2023-12-20.
checks.qualification: This confirms a historical regional price, not the current tariff. The numerical scenario uses a sourced planning input pending a current quote.

checks.topic: Oregon gp3 price and included performance
checks.unit: USD per provisioned GB-month, IOPS, MB/s, seconds
checks.approved_wording: AWS's Oregon example prices gp3 storage at $0.08 per GB-month. Included performance is 3,000 IOPS and 125 MB/s.
checks.locator: WorkSpaces managed instances pricing examples 1 and 2. EBS gp3 pricing example and billing paragraph.
checks.qualification: Storage is provisioned capacity, billed per second with a sixty-second minimum until released. Additional IOPS or throughput incurs additional charges.

checks.approved_wording: AWS examples price S3 Standard GET and HEAD requests at $0.0004 per thousand. PUT and LIST examples use $0.005 per thousand.
checks.locator: Spark blog Amazon S3 request cost table. PostgreSQL blog Cost considerations table.
checks.qualification: The Spark example omits its region. The PostgreSQL example names North Virginia. These are Oregon planning proxies, not verified current Oregon tariffs.

checks.topic: S3 Standard storage tier price anchors
checks.unit: USD per GiB-month, S3 Standard, North Virginia example
checks.approved_wording: An AWS North Virginia example lists S3 Standard tiers of $0.023, $0.022, and $0.021 per GB-month.
checks.locator: SAP blog Cost Consideration, region introduction and Amazon S3 row. S3 Pricing Details defines binary storage units.
checks.qualification: Tiers cover the first 50 TiB, next 450 TiB, and storage above 500 TiB. Oregon use is a regional planning proxy.

checks.unit: USD per transferred GB and GB per month
checks.approved_wording: S3 internet ingress and transfers to AWS services in the same region have no transfer charge. Same-region bucket transfers are also free.
checks.locator: Data transfer, list of transfers without a charge.
checks.qualification: Requests and compute remain billable. Internet egress's first 100 GB is aggregated across AWS services and regions, excluding China and GovCloud.

checks.topic: S3 gateway endpoint cost and reach
checks.approved_wording: An S3 gateway endpoint has no additional charge. It permits VPC access to same-region S3 without an internet gateway or NAT device.
checks.locator: Opening explanation and Considerations, region requirement.
checks.qualification: This does not provide arbitrary internet access for catalog queries. Interface endpoints, NAT routing, and cross-region routes have different cost conditions.

checks.unit: USD per GB-second, USD per million requests, and MiB
checks.approved_wording: AWS Lambda pricing examples use $0.0000166667 per x86 GB-second and $0.20 per million requests. Additional ephemeral storage costs $0.0000000309 per GB-second.
checks.locator: On-Demand pricing examples, especially example 3 and its ephemeral-storage calculation.
checks.qualification: Examples use North Virginia. Oregon rates remain planning proxies. The first 512 MiB of ephemeral storage is included. Free tiers and discounts are separate.

checks.unit: seconds, MiB, concurrent invocations, environments per ten seconds, and Mbps
checks.approved_wording: Ordinary Lambda invocations have a 900-second limit and up to 10,240 MiB of memory. Default network bandwidth is 625 Mbps per environment.
checks.locator: Compute and storage, Function configuration, deployment, and execution.
checks.qualification: New accounts have lower quotas. Non-VPC functions can request increased bandwidth, reaching up to 3,000 Mbps at maximum memory. Memory allocation controls CPU.

checks.approved_wording: Linux EC2 On-Demand instances are billed per second with a sixty-second minimum, from launch until stopped or terminated.
checks.qualification: This does not eliminate startup, idle, or shutdown time. Attached EBS continues accruing storage charges until released.

checks.unit: USD per GB-second, Ohio x86 example published 2022-08-04
checks.approved_wording: AWS's Ohio x86 example discounts monthly duration above six billion GB-seconds, with another tier above fifteen billion GB-seconds.
checks.locator: Tiered pricing announcement, Ohio example. Current pricing overview describes aggregation by architecture and region.
checks.qualification: Historical Ohio rates do not verify current Oregon rates. Tiers apply to monthly usage, not a multimonth backfill total, and separate architectures and regions.

checks.approved_wording: S3 storage pricing uses binary gigabytes and terabytes. One billed GB is 2^30 bytes, and one billed TB is 2^40 bytes.
checks.locator: S3 Pricing Details and storage-unit note preceding Replication.
checks.qualification: Use GiB and TiB labels in scenario outputs to prevent confusion with decimal transfer volumes.

checks.topic: EC2 c7i.xlarge sustained and burst networking
checks.approved_wording: AWS lists c7i.xlarge networking at 1.562 Gbps baseline and 12.5 Gbps burst. Bursting depends on network credits.
checks.locator: Compute optimized Network specifications, c7i.xlarge row. Network bandwidth guide, baseline and burst explanation.
checks.qualification: Baseline converts to 195.25 decimal MB/s per instance before protocol overhead. Concurrent workers share this capacity. Advertised burst bandwidth is unsuitable for sustained backfill assumptions.

limitations: Research and checking occurred in separate agents. Neither checked documentation nor numerical modeling establishes measured AWS performance.
No current Oregon price export was verified. Several rates are explicitly historical or proxies from other regions.
Population anchors have different size and eligibility filters. None establishes the scenario's complete permanent-water population down to ten meters.
Population, shoreline, occupied tiles, compression, observation frequency, processing throughput, and sample variability remain planning assumptions where not measured.
The independent check confirms only the qualified claims recorded here. It does not approve a production platform or grant owner approval.
